correctness.rationale: In one-based ruler indices the letter is 1+v2(j); two occurrences of a maximal valuation in a linear interval would have a higher valuation between them. Thus any circular square crosses the original cut. Palindromicity gives the square starting at N-d. For an off-center square, reflection puts the cut inside the second half: with x>0 letters of that half before the cut and y>0 after it, equality of the two Parikh vectors forces P(y+2x)-P(y)=2P(x). The contiguous factor on the left contains an index divisible by 2^r for r=floor(log2 x)+1, since its length is 2x; the prefix on the right has no such letter. This excludes off-center squares. A square survives exactly the cuts d<=c<=N-d, including its endpoints; a cube would give two distinct square starts at the same half-length. The base order has no admissible square. An independent carry-free integer encoding with doubled-word prefix sums verified exact occurrence pairs, all cut counts and absence of cubes through order 9, plus the length-21 counterexample.
